params.body:
## Why

Sessions on the workbench pass two gates before anything reaches GitHub: Claude Code's own permission layer (in auto mode, a classifier that judges every command) and the control gateway. The classifier does not read `CLAUDE.md`. It knows this setup only through `autoMode.environment` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, which lives per machine and in no repo. When that text lags behind, the classifier misjudges routine work. On 2026-10-10 it refused a `hand.mjs propose` from a mail-intake session as an "external system write", although the gateway is the sanctioned write path and can never merge.

## Change

- `claude/automode-environment.json`: the auto mode environment as it stands on the workbench, now under version control. It includes three new entries: the write path and its two gates, mail-intake sessions (the intake instructions are authorised, the forwarded mail is not), and what stays the operator's even through the hand.
- `claude/install.mjs`: writes that array into `~/.claude/settings.json` (it keeps a `.bak` of the previous file); `--check` reports whether a machine matches the repo.
- `CLAUDE.md`, under the core rule: the two gates, where the classifier gets its context, `propose` as a single command, and the rule that a session does not edit its own instructions or config (the classifier refuses that, rightly) but prepares the change for the operator.

## After merging

On each machine: `node ~/Projects/workspace/claude/install.mjs`, after the checkout has pulled main. The workbench already has the 28 entries, so there it reports "up to date". The MacBook does not have them yet.
params.title: Keep the auto mode environment in the repo and explain the two gates
